title: Feature: Global workspace sync for multi-monitor setups
head: d8990d9f15f7
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Custom XDG_STATE_HOME separates Lua's toggle directory from the flag checked by every new consumer
leads.consequence: When XDG_STATE_HOME is set to a nondefault path, omarchy-hyprland-toggle workspace-global on writes HOME/.local/state, while Hyprland requires toggle files from XDG_STATE_HOME/omarchy/toggles/hypr. Hyprland never installs the workspace.active hook/rules, yet new key wrappers and bar believe global mode is on. The global switch falls back to a raw slot when the bases file is absent (bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-switch:27-33), so monitors do not synchronize. Use the same resolved state path in producer, Lua loader and new consumers.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator: loader uses XDG_STATE_HOME and toggle CLI uses HOME/.local/state at base too; pre-existing for all toggles, not introduced by PR. Dropped.

leads.summary: Turning on global workspaces replaces a user's existing workspace-to-monitor rules
leads.consequence: A user rule for workspace 1 with monitor=DP-1 loaded from ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua is loaded before toggles. The new code registers another rule for workspace 1 with monitor set to the auto-allocated monitor (eDP-1 if first), and Hyprland merges by identical workspaceString with later nonempty monitor taking precedence. The user's pinned workspace is silently re-bound. Preserve/consult existing user rules, or document that global mode explicitly overrides them.
leads.triage: behavioural, sent to Opus (followup-1 Q1): minor, inherent to feature. Not published.

leads.summary: Turning the mode off hides occupied high-ID workspaces from the bar and numbered shortcuts
leads.consequence: With a window on global workspace 12, disabling global mode only removes the toggle file and reloads Hyprland, it neither moves windows to local IDs nor restores a navigation route. Local keybindings target IDs 1-10, and the bar's local slotOfId(12) is 12, rejected by workspaceIds' 1-10 filter. Hyprland's reload clears rules, not occupied workspaces. The window persists but disappears from the bar and numbered shortcuts. SUPER+TAB can still cycle over existing workspaces, including that window's ID (Hyprland MiscFunctions.cpp:380-447), but discovering it becomes difficult. Provide a reversal/migration step or keep occupied IDs visible in local mode.
leads.triage: behavioural, Opus Q2: minor; hidden from bar/SUPER+N but reachable via SUPER+TAB. Not published (REPORT).

leads.summary: Window mover snapshots the active window address but dispatches against the then-current active window
leads.consequence: If focus changes between activewindow -j and the final dispatch (there are monitor and Python JSON round trips), the first address only acts as a presence check. Hyprland's omitted window selector resolves the focused window at dispatch time, so a rapid focus change can move a different window. Supply window = 'address:<snapshot>' in the Lua move table if the original active window still exists; if targeting the current focus is intentional, omit the unused snapshot instead.

leads.summary: Bar maps unrelated positive workspace IDs into global slots
leads.consequence: With saved bases {eDP-1:0,HDMI-A-1:10} and an existing user-created workspace 101 containing windows, maxKnownId becomes 101 and slotOfId(101) returns 1. Thus slot 1 looks occupied even though neither global slot-1 workspace contains its windows; clicking it calls omarchy-switch-to-aw 1, which dispatches mapped IDs 1/11, not 101. Unlike the Lua slot_of guard, the bar does not check that an ID belongs to any saved base range. Read/track the bases map when computing occupancy and workspaceIds.
leads.triage: behavioural, Opus Q3: minor, only via user actions. Not published.

leads.summary: Upgrading fixes to the shipped Lua toggle does not upgrade an already-enabled user's copy
leads.consequence: Enabling copies default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua into personal state. On package upgrade only the packaged default changes; the loader executes the old copied file. Refresh Hyprland copies flags.lua only; no new migration replaces workspace-global.lua. A user who enabled an early revision will keep its earlier behavior after this PR is upgraded, until they run toggle off/on or manually replace the copy. Introduce a safe migration, or use an enabled marker that loads the current packaged implementation while preserving any personal modifications.
leads.triage: pre-existing toggle-copy mechanism for all toggles, not PR-specific. Dropped.

leads.summary: New local move test asserts silent behavior for a follow move, so it fails at head before global cases
leads.consequence: The test runs omarchy-move-window-to-aw 3 without --silent. Production deliberately omits follow=false in that branch (lines 38-44), and the hyprctl stub merely echoes its arguments (test:24-28). The assertion on line 64 therefore always calls fail and exits before global routing at lines 67-79 is tested. Rewrite this assertion to expect the absence of follow=false, and add a separate --silent case asserting its presence.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (R5-move-window-to-aw-test still present). Corroboration.

leads.summary: Failed monitor enumeration dispatches to saved disconnected monitor bases
leads.consequence: On a transient nonzero/invalid hyprctl monitors -j response, live_monitors=None and the loop dispatches every persisted base, including disconnected outputs (retained intentionally). Their workspace focus can create a stray workspace on another monitor and steal focus; the final focused-monitor dispatch repairs focus only when that name resolves. Avoid broadening to saved disconnected monitors on an enumeration error, fail with a clear status or query the focused monitor only. Tests' failed-activeworkspace stub does not produce a valid monitors JSON and currently expects all bases, so it enshrines this behavior.
leads.triage: fallback already described as Verified behavior in R5. Dropped.

leads.summary: Updated switch tests cannot detect removal of the disconnected-monitor filter
leads.consequence: All three saved bases in the test also occur in the successful monitors stub. Deleting the production `if live_monitors ... continue` (global-switch:80-82) leaves every assertion unchanged. Its error case explicitly expects all three after an invalid monitors reply. Add one persisted but unplugged name in the fixture and assert no dispatch to that base on a successful monitor query, with an explicit separate error-response assertion.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (mutant M2). Corroboration; published as optional test improvement.

leads.summary: No menu entry or manual instructions expose how to enable the opt-in mode
leads.consequence: The new toggle file ships under default/hypr/toggles but is not enabled by install, and the feature is not included in the Toggle menu near Workspace Layout or described in the manual. Users who do not know the private `omarchy-hyprland-toggle workspace-global` command cannot discover or enable the feature through the normal UI; menu action and documentation would provide a supported opt-in/out path.

limits: Source-derived conditional behavior has not been exercised in a live Hyprland session, none reserved. Only CLI metadata check and a bash control were run under review.py. Other test cases inferred from their actual stubs/assertions, not claimed as executed.

The compare API for forked open PR head commits returned 404 in related-N.stack; no merged-code or stacking conclusion is reported. Related diff receipts and 209-file current-base comparison are preserved under this directory.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5855518237) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5856740667), checked at `d8990d9f15f7`.

**Outcome:** three previous findings are resolved and one is partly resolved. `move-window-to-aw-test.sh` still fails: the commit meant for it edited a different test file. Two new findings: the SUPER+CTRL+TAB change also alters that key for every multi-monitor user in local mode, and the last commit adds 241 unrelated files (about 10.7 MB) to the repository root.

**Verified:** the tester installer is removed, the new count checks work, and the SUPER+CTRL+TAB change fixes global mode (modelled, not a native run).

| Previous finding | Status at `d8990d9f15f7` |
|---|---|
| `move-window-to-aw-test.sh` fails | **Still present** (see below) |
| Tester installer ships as `tools/install.sh` | **Resolved.** Removed; no `tools/` directory remains |
| SUPER+CTRL+TAB in global mode | **Resolved** for global mode (modelled, not a native run). The change also applies to local mode (see below) |
| Optional test: count check in section 1b | **Resolved.** A mutant that reorders the silent binding's modifiers and drops `--silent` now fails the head test and passes the previous one |
| Optional test: `monitors -j` stub for the switch test | **Partly resolved** (see the test note below) |

**Verified:** apart from line 38 of `default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua`, no runtime file changed since `e0c507e9ac07`. The findings from earlier reviews that were recorded as resolved stay resolved, except the SUPER+TAB range-edge case corrected below. In isolated runs, `./test/cli` passes, and `./test/shell` fails on the same set of files at this head as at `e0c507e9ac07`. Of those files, only `move-window-to-aw-test.sh` belongs to this PR; the others fail identically at both heads, in files this PR does not touch, mostly on missing sandbox prerequisites.

## New in this revision

### The SUPER+CTRL+TAB change also applies in local mode

[`tiling.lua:38`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/d8990d9f15f71bfdc579d2ba329bc69428b646c6/default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua#L38) now binds `focus({ workspace = "previous_per_monitor" })` for everyone, not only when `workspace-global` is enabled. In Hyprland 0.56.2, `previous_per_monitor` returns only the most recent other workspace in history that was on the focused monitor (`ConfigActions.cpp` `resolveWorkspaceForChange`, `WorkspaceHistoryTracker.cpp`). If there is none, the dispatch fails with a logged warning and nothing happens.

```text
Modelled from Hyprland 0.56.2 source, toggle off, not a native run.
Two monitors: A shows 1 (focused), B shows 2.
                                   base ("previous")        this head ("previous_per_monitor")
SUPER+2, then SUPER+CTRL+TAB       back to 1 on A           no change, focus stays on B
```

In the model, with a single monitor the two selectors behave the same.

**Impact:** for multi-monitor users who never enable global mode, "Jump to former workspace" (the wording in `manual/07-hotkeys.md`) no longer returns to a workspace on another monitor. Depending on that monitor's history, it either does nothing or switches the current monitor to one of its own earlier workspaces. The previous review suggested this selector for global mode only.

**Suggested change:** keep `"previous"` in `tiling.lua`, and have `workspace-global.lua` rebind the key while the toggle is on, for example `o.rebind("SUPER + CTRL + TAB", "Former workspace", hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = "previous_per_monitor" }))`. Toggles load after the default bindings (`config/hypr/hyprland.lua`). If the change for all users is intended, call it out as a default change.

### The last commit adds 241 unrelated files to the repository root

[`d8990d9f`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/commit/d8990d9f15f71bfdc579d2ba329bc69428b646c6) ("test: add count checks and monitor JSON stub for optional improvements") also adds:

- 10 Markdown working notes, including `STATUS.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` and `FINDINGS_SEP9_2026.md`. Some describe an earlier head, and some refer to a different PR (#10199).
- A browser-saved copy of this PR's GitHub page (`2026-09-24 Pull Request #12978 comments from llstrk.html`), plus its 230-file asset directory of GitHub JavaScript, CSS, emoji and avatar images.

Together they add about 10.7 MB. They have no runtime effect: neither package built from this repository (`omarchy`, `omarchy-settings`) copies them, and no test reads root files.

**Impact:** a merge would put third-party web assets and personal notes into the tree and history of every clone. The commit message does not mention them, and the repository's `AGENTS.md` asks for atomic commits that do not mix unrelated work.

**Suggested change:** remove these files from the branch.

## Still present

### `move-window-to-aw-test.sh` still fails (test-only)

Commit `247dbf3e` changed a pass message in `workspace-global-move-window-test.sh`. That file tests the global helper, which always passes `follow = false`, so it was already correct. The failing file, [`move-window-to-aw-test.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/d8990d9f15f71bfdc579d2ba329bc69428b646c6/test/shell.d/move-window-to-aw-test.sh#L58-L66), is unchanged. It still calls `omarchy-move-window-to-aw 3` without `--silent` and expects `follow = false`:

```text
Isolated run, same result at e0c507e9ac07 and at this head:
got: hyprctl dispatch hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = "3" })
not ok - local mode passes follow=false for silent move
```

**Impact:** `./test/shell` still reports this failure. Runtime behavior is unaffected.

**Suggested change:** call `omarchy-move-window-to-aw --silent 3` in that check. In an isolated run, a copy with that one change passes all 10 checks in the file.

## Test note and correction

**Optional test improvement:** the switch-test stub now answers `monitors -j`, but it reports exactly the three saved monitors, so the live-monitor filter never skips anything. With the filter disabled, the switch test still passes all 9 checks. Adding a monitor that is saved but not reported by `monitors -j`, and asserting that its workspace (for example `22`) is not dispatched, would catch that regression. With such a stub, the head helper dispatches `12, 2` and the filter-disabled copy dispatches `12, 22, 2`.

**Correction to the previous review:** it stated that the Lua hook keeps focus on the current monitor for SUPER+TAB. That holds away from range edges, but not at them. With two monitors, SUPER+TAB from slot 10 on the base-0 monitor goes to workspace 11, which belongs to the other monitor. Hyprland focuses that monitor before the hook runs, so the hook keeps focus there, and every monitor ends on slot 1. SUPER+SHIFT+TAB at the opposite edge is the mirror case. This is source-derived only, not modelled or observed natively. A native two-monitor check would settle it.

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned-source inspection of `d8990d9f15f7` against `e0c507e9ac07` and the base, with Hyprland 0.56.2 source and the Omarchy packaging recipe. Isolated command runs covered the full `./test/shell` and `./test/cli` suites at both heads, the seven PR test files, targeted mutants of the workspace bindings and the switch helper, a one-line fix to `move-window-to-aw-test.sh`, and a model of Hyprland's workspace history for SUPER+CTRL+TAB. No native Hyprland, multi-monitor or keybinding test was run. The added HTML page and notes were read as text only. The SUPER+CTRL+TAB results are modelled, and the SUPER+TAB edge correction is source-derived.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
